cards.title: Your Body-Clock Anchor (BioTime)
cards.summary: Your body-clock anchor sits around 06:06 — a night-owl (late) type, ~1.3 h later than the population average (±1.0 h). Your heart-rate circadian minimum independently lands near 05:33, confirming the anchor physiologically. This is where your clock sits — how consistently you hit it is a separate question (see regularity).

cards.title: Your Sleep Schedule Is Somewhat Irregular
cards.summary: Your sleep schedule is **moderately irregular** (SRI 78/100, 28-day). Your bedtime swings ±0.4 h night to night and sleep length varies ±1.3 h. Your body-clock anchor still reads stable (~06:06) because you compensate — going to bed late, you sleep in — which holds the midpoint fixed while your actual bed and wake times scatter. The anchor is where your clock wants to be; the irregularity is the cost your body pays to hit it.

cards.title: BioTime Shifted in 2025-12
cards.summary: In 2025-12 your body-clock anchor ran 0.9 h later (evening-shifted) than your prior baseline — your sleep midpoint moved from ~05:18 to ~06:11 (95% CI +0.4 to +1.3 h, 28 nights). This is drift measured against your OWN recent normal, not the population.
